verification_rule: verified=true only when the quoted statement was read on the page at source_url on 2026-10-09; false means search snippet, unreadable page, or inference

claims.claim: Report 12 (18 Jul 2026) flags sheet switches by projecting the 3D vector between two points with the same 2D coordinates onto each patch's surface normal and thresholding its length; patches are 180-500 vox diameter at 4-vox quadmesh spacing (1.7-4.7 mm at 9.362 um).

Report 12: Scroll 4 56,968 patches, 9,171 bad (16%); PHerc0139 2,858 patches, 456 bad, 19 bridges; a 3-winding unwrapping 'mostly free from sheet switching problems'; method 'doesn't make any assumption about it being a rolled up sheet'.

Report 10 (27 Dec 2025): 94,142 Scroll 4 patches, 1,153 problem patches at a 3D distance threshold of 50; a missed case diverged by no more than 41 units; false positives and manually found false negatives acknowledged.

pipeline9: 'c' outputs badpatches.csv, 'n' runs simulated annealing, 'v' outputs badbridges_out.csv (patches connecting others with implausibly different 2D coords); inputs are a surface-prediction OME-Zarr (level 0) and a volume OME-Zarr (level 2); parameters.json is set up for PHerc0139.

Winners page: Jul 2026 $2,500 to William Stevens 'Identifies and removes problem areas that cause sheet switching, leaving a scaffolding of known-good patches'; Aug 2026 $20,000 'Detects when the 2D alignments of overlapping patches imply incompatible 3D locations, drops the offending patches'.

vc_tifxyz_selfcross reports where a tifxyz passes through itself; both-diagonal triangulation; transverse contacts only count; no distance threshold; --exclude default 1; --maxedge default 60 voxels; exit 3 with --fail-on-crossing; deterministic across thread counts.

windcheck: 274/274 traces clean under both canonical triangulations after repair, checked with vc_tifxyz_selfcross across 456,475,808 triangles; area-weighted retention 0.994566; 84,316 PHercParis4 patches audited, five self-intersect; 'Nothing here establishes which physical sheet a surface belongs to.'

vc_tifxyz_topology (PR #1884, Draft, opened 24 Sep 2026, not merged) counts islands, holes, tears and folds (triangles facing >120 degrees apart); PHerc0009B census 7 components and 1,423 island quads matched vc_flatten dropping 2,846 triangles; 829 of 907 published tifxyz in 145.6 s.

tifxyz-doctor audits per-cell Jacobian condition, symmetric stretch, area ratio, shear, symmetric Dirichlet energy, adjacent-cell normal jumps; v0.2 cue localized 124/128 abrupt 8-voxel and 128/128 abrupt 16-voxel normal-offset proxies on a 128-patch holdout; gradual transitions mostly missed; no labeled corpus of correct/incorrect geometry.

vc_calc_surface_metrics outputs surface_missing_fraction, winding_error_fraction and in_surface_metric from a VC3D point collection annotated with relative winding numbers; inter-winding points go along the surface normal across several windings; winding.tif from vc_tifxyz_winding; no thresholds given.

vc_tifxyz_winding: 500 random ray seeds along grid normals, 1,000 candidates each, hit if point-to-line distance <= 0.5, duplicates within 4 px dropped, per-winding spacing = median per 400-px band, pair accepted if |dx - ref| <= ref/3, propagation from one seed; FIXME says propagation runs one way only; no umbilicus read.

Oct 2025 post: GrowPatch normal alignment loss uses 'a fast approximate skeletonization trace of surface prediction slices'; snapping loss 'Based on the same skeletonization as the normals'; direction-field term 'penalizes deviation from a dense direction field' from fiber predictions or structure tensor orientations; symmetric Dirichlet barrier; corrections 'reduce sheet switches'.

Point corrections for vc_grow_seg_from_seed are applied with --resume and --correct; the solver keeps the area around the convex hull of the correction points; no validation steps documented; normal grids must exist (vc_compute_normal_grids) or be streamed via normal-grids-remote.json.
Feb 2025 post: in an ~800 cm2 Scroll 5 crop sheet jumps went from 'around 11' (by eye) to 0 in just over two weeks; Scroll 5's top is crushed and 'the prediction quality is relatively poor'.

copy_displacement_latest predicts a 3-vector displacement field from a conditioning mesh to the recto surface of the winding in front of and behind it; 'trained at 4.8um resolution, but performs ok at 2.4um and 9.6um'; no evaluation numbers on the card.

PR #1284 (merged 17 Aug 2026) adds --displacement-scale auto = training voxel size / inference voxel size; motivating benchmark on one 7.91 um Scroll 3 window: wrong-hop rate 63.17% -> 5.90% (front, n=4,697) and 56.28% -> 7.73% (back, n=8,697); described as 'a local geometric benchmark rather than ground truth'.
The exact rule by which a hop is judged wrong in issue #1149 is in a linked log that was not read.

nnInteractive refinement: one mask covering all sheets -> one label per sheet via cc3d face connectivity, erosion split of bridged sheets, prompts (mask, flanking gap centrelines negative, own centreline positive); JSON reports per-sheet voxel counts and Dice vs input; no validation results reported.

arXiv 2512.04927 (Henderson, WACV 2026): Archimedean spiral deformed by per-slice affine, integrated flow field and gap-scaling field; metrics WJF, MRWD, ChD, AD, Str; Paris 4 (7.91 um, ~30 GT windings): ChD 5.29 vs 5.59, AD 0.0568 vs 0.1567, Str 1.239 vs 1.027 vs ThaumatoAnakalyptor; MRWD 25.67 without relative-winding loss vs 7.64; limitations 'the surface sometimes wanders between two true windings' and 'We also currently assume the scroll is a single rolled sheet.'; code at github.com/pmh47/spiral-fitting.

Spiral tutorial: umbilicus required; losses include verified patches ('a verified patch should coincide with a single winding across its whole extent'), relative/absolute winding annotations, tracks, normals, gradient magnitude ('local winding density'); outputs wNNN and wNNN_spliced tifxyz plus satisfaction_metrics_fitted.json; 'Only human-checked (verified) patches are recommended; they are also used to calculate evaluation metrics.'

villa/spiral-fitting README: --dataset must contain umbilicus.json and spiral-scroll.json (voxel_size_um required, 'no validation beyond presence'); extract_surface_tracks.py binarizes predictions, slabs 4 voxels deep every 16 z-voxels and vertical slabs every 64 voxels, skeletonizes, chains >= 10 vertices become tracks; losses include radius, DT snap, Lasagna normals/gradient magnitude, native minimum-spacing, winding_model pairs (24,000 samples/step), fiber-direction (off by default).

8 Oct 2026: $50K First Letters Prize to Erwin Nieuwlaar for PHerc. 343 on the 8.64 um scan using the open-source spiral fitter adapted by him with 'his own estimate of the scroll axis (umbilicus)', a new way 'to snap the segments more accurately to the papyrus surface', windings w047 and w048 joined across theta=0; four 9 um ink models averaged; criteria '10 readable letters in 4cm2'.

pherc343-first-letters mesh/README: villa spiral chain commit 0fb38c45 on z 9500-11000 with inputs/umbilicus_PHerc0343.json; distance field from m7 surface prediction at level 1 threshold 128; 'snap_meshes.py (defaults, level 0)' 'moves every node along its normal onto the nearest predicted sheet'; lasagna flatten_fast_nofilter.json; no quality checks or metrics reported.

pherc343-first-letters top README: volume 20250521140437-8.640um-1.2m-116keV-masked.zarr; 66-layer render one voxel apart; reproducibility checks only (bit-identical meshes and images; ink map r 0.99999 between GPUs); no cross-section or surface-correctness metric.

PR #1745 (closed, not merged, 14 Sep 2026): umbilicus files for PHerc0191, 0257, 0268, 0358, 0800, 0813 are 'estimates, not tracings'; 'PHerc0800 and PHerc0268 have umbilicus files but no validated count yet'.
Prizes page lists PHerc0268 volume 20251110183117 as eligible: 2027 Grand Prize entry 5 of 13, First Letters entry 7 of 22; no voxel size stated there.
A third-party atlas repository calls PHerc0268 'the foggiest eligible scan' with 42% foggy profiles.

ScrollFiesta submission.pdf: identity carried as 'sheet tracks whose pairwise integer winding relations compose through a maximum-support forest with integer subtree-shift loop closure, so geometry is never fused to make an order graph connected'; welding joins fronts 'only where both cubes agree on the wrap'; two-sided generalized winding number + integer-label MRF by alpha-beta swap graph cuts.

ScrollFiesta numbers (PHerc0139): 4x5x5 block 882,219 vertices, 783 components -> 25, energy 221.369 -> 200.486, continuation/order satisfaction 0.99971/0.99816 in 10.8 s; 213-cube 15,457 tracks over 112 winds at 5.0% residual conflict weight; GWN unit jump at 310,686 of 313,615 vertices (99.1%); 'a slab splitter that separates 0 of 246 fused runs'; unguarded penalty run 'winding span expands from 14.13 to 32.41 turns'; public config 47.4% coverage, 171 overlapping triangle pairs, reported as unqualified.

docs/PIPELINE.md: per-cube multi-winding gate needs scroll geometry (PHerc0139 calibration --umb-y 3405 --umb-x 2878 --wrap-pitch 9.5); seam evidence 6,441 seam pairs and 2.98% whole-turn error with zero inset vs 2,713 pairs and 15.78% with one-voxel inset; 'Treat a failing registration or seam audit as a failed run'.

Winners page: ScrollFiesta prizes May 2026 $10,000, Jul 2026 $20,000, Aug 2026 $2,500 ('A retrained 9 um surface model distilled from 2.4 um predictions'); Jul 2026 $1,000 Josep Carreras windcheck; Jul 2026 $1,000 Aviad Cohen tifxyz-doctor; Aug 2026 $1,000 Benjamin Hamm nnInteractive refinement; Aug 2026 $1,000 Mihajlo Nestorovic 'A trained 3D model that grows a single papyrus sheet from a seed' (no link).

PR #1930 (merged 5 Oct 2026): Automated Fiber Volumes (.afv) are read-only SQLite containers with an RTree over blocks of <= 256 segments; PHerc. 0175A collection 61,486 fibers, 3.9 GB; VC3D opens an .afv in under 1 ms vs ~8 min JSON import for 300k+ fibers.

PR #1934 (open, 30 Sep 2026): .afv generator uses nnU-Net model Qualzz20/afv_fiber_9um on 512^3 blocks, skeletonizes and fits polylines, joins aligned ends up to 30 voxels apart, cuts joins turning more than 45 degrees, removes fibers shorter than 100 voxels; example on a 9.362 um PHerc. 0813 zone: 1,055 fibers (1.87 m) in 1 min 21 s on one RTX 3090; checked for identical polylines against the ported code.

Line annotation doc: spans filled by native 3D fiber trace, Lasagna normal optimisation or cubic spline; merge accepted when error <= max(10 base voxels, 10% of combined traced length); span actions 'Split, different windings' and 'Split and link, same winding'; no accuracy numbers.

Fiber intersections: broad phase by Euclidean segment distance (maxDistance default 2000 vx) then one Ceres refinement per candidate with point-distance and sign-ambiguous normal-orthogonality residuals; results not persisted; atlas decisions 'same winding (h inside v)', 'different winding', 'hard to say' (default), only the first appends a link with desired_winding_delta = 0.

Atlas: winding = floor((atlasU - zero_winding_column) / period_columns); links.json constraint actual_winding(second) - actual_winding(first) = desired_winding_delta; flood-fill integer offsets from a root fiber; 'conflicting cycles are reported by the returned conflict list and debug log while the deterministic flood-fill assignment remains in place'.

June 2026 progress post: semi-automated fiber tracing in Lasagna lets 'an annotator can trace a fiber at the speed of 2 cm / minute' where the latent holds; 'We are close to saturating the performance of models trained on the approximate surface labels our annotators can produce.'; 'our representations still struggle in some of the most densely packed regions, which are not rare.'; Neural Tracing 'soon drifts off the intended surface'.

FASP (Jan 2025 changelog): patch growing with vc_grow_seg_from_seed, large-area tracer with a consensus data term, winding assignment that places random points, measures intersections along normals and diffuses a consistent winding number from a single seed; rendered from half-resolution volumes (7.91 um metadata); ~28 h compute + 4 h human; no numeric accuracy.

SCROLL_ANATOMY.md: 'A fold bends papyrus back onto itself and can involve one or several windings.'; 'A sharp bend is not necessarily a fold.'; 'Near the core of a roll, papyrus may fold back on itself one or more times'; 'Compression can bring adjacent windings into contact, reduce or eliminate the space between them'; no numbers, no hairpin term.

Kaggle Surface Detection scoring (13 Nov 2025 post): 'A topology-aware linear blend rewarding both voxel accuracy and surface connectivity', penalising 'no gaps, holes, sheet-switches or mergers'; no formula given.
The Kaggle metric is a blend of Surf Dice, VOI and Topo score components.

19 Mar 2026 post: Kaggle ended; 'Almost all of the top 10 submissions used large ensembles of our baseline, a ResEncUNet trained with the nn-UNet framework.'; holes addressed with post-processing; Lasagna semi-global optimisation of adjacent wraps is experimental; VC3D streams remote volumes.

surface_m7_nnunet card: Dataset100_VesuviusSurface, 786 training volumes, nnUNetResEncUNetLPlans, 3d_fullres 192x192x192 patches, labels 0/1/2 (ignore); no scrolls, voxel size, loss or evaluation numbers.

Geometry-stratified diagnostic: per-bin AUC of P(surface) at GT points vs near-sheet background 2-10 vox; one model 0.413 at <4 vox compression vs 0.886 at >22 vox; 'This is not the official Kaggle Surface Detection metric'.

15 Aug 2025 post: dense sheets appear in a 'fog' hypothesised to come from microscopic periodic fibre structures; best 0.55 um settings 7 cm, 65 keV; 2.4 um settings 22 cm, 77 keV; phase retrieval 'seems to be beneficial for segmentation and unwrapping'; no quantitative metric.

arXiv 2606.29085: nnU-Net-style 3D U-Net with Medial Surface Recall loss as an intermediate cue; tifxyz quad meshes grown from seeds; mesh-offset tool traces rays from an existing mesh; 'Regions judged to be a single sheet receive an approval mask'; geometric inpainting 'did not create tomographic intensity values, ink signal, or image evidence'; SLIM flattening; 65 layers at 1-voxel spacing at 2.4 um; '~25 hours per wrap of manual annotation'; acceptance 'geometrically tight to the papyrus layer'; code commit e583fb6.

Prizes page 2027 Grand Prize: '100% of the papyrus recto surface unrolled.'; 'Each tifxyz must already include a low-distortion isometric 2D parametrization (flattening).'; 'up to 8 documented hours of human annotation / input are tolerated.'; Stage-1 guidance 'check if you can visually follow horizontal papyrus fibers across the page'; First Letters 'you must demonstrate that the text is not hallucinated'.

18 Aug 2026 workflow post: 'A good surface stays on one papyrus sheet instead of jumping to its neighbor.'; 'continuous horizontal and vertical papyrus fibers are a strong sign that the geometry is following the sheet correctly.'; 'In areas with strong local distortions the ink models can become confused and produce things that look very letter-like.'; 'never train on the region you intend to claim as a discovery'.

Winding constraints page (updated 12 Jul 2026): same-winding, relative-winding and absolute-winding constraint types; 'There is no required annotation tool or generation method.'; no quantitative evaluation protocol; current dataset spiral-input 2026-07 for PHercParis4 (~27,000 verified and ~204,000 unverified patches).

2026 open problems page: surface prediction 'does not tell us which voxels belong to the same sheet'; sheet switches handled by VC3D inspection and manual correction; 'No method yet traces a complete, correct surface through a scroll automatically.'; tools listed: GrowPatch (Ceres), Copy Out/In, copy_displacement_latest, Lasagna, flatboi (SLIM), fiber_hz_vt, fit_spiral.py.
